newsitem.title: USA: Mobil says turnarounds lopped $65 mln off Q1.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says turnarounds lopped $65 mln off Q1.

text.p: Mobil Corp first quarter per share operating income rose to $2.11 from $1.83 a year ago as operating earnings rose 15 percent to $844 million from $736 million, despite high refinery maintenance activity in the quarter.

"U.S. marketing and refining experienced a high concentration of scheduled refinery turnarounds in the first quarter which negatively impacted net results by about $65 million. The scheduled turnarounds are essentially complete for the year and all refineries are operating normally," said chief executive Lucio Noto.

Worldwide refining and marketing operating earnings fell $90 million to $150 million as U.S. operations lost $42 million compared with a $59 million profit in the 1996 quarter as four out of five refineries had turnarounds.
International refining and marketing rose $11 million to $192 million due to increase fuel margins in the UK and lower downtime costs.
Weaker refining margins in Asia Pacific and lower aromatics income in Singapore offset some of the other gains.
International E&P earnings rose $113 million to $470 million as realised crude prices rose to $20.92 from $18.57 and natgas climbed to $3.06 per mcf from $2.51.
Liquids rose 100 trillion barrels to 553 trillion and natgas rose 60 million cubic feet to 3,687 million.

"International upstream volumes increased, reflecting successful development programs in West Africa and last year's acquisitions of Ampolex and an interest in the Tengiz field in the Republic of Kazakstan. Natural gas production was also higher in Germany, primarily to meet new demand in the former East Germany," Noto said.
